how_to_fix: Treat the previous active work as cut off: inspect any durable evidence or partial product changes, but do not assume the stale claim is live ownership.
Start by reading this lifecycle.open_repair_plan_2026_07_03, lifecycle.remediation_appendage, lifecycle.operator_decision_summary, scope.acceptance_criteria, and scope.proof_targets before editing.

Inspect the current product/runtime files named by the audit note before deciding whether the defect still exists; existing implementation_result PASS/PROVEN language is not official validation evidence.
If the defect still exists, make the smallest live-path fix that closes the named operator-visible/runtime gap; if current code already fixed it, do not rework it, instead rerun and record the proof.
Map the fix back to the contract acceptance criteria (AC-108-1, AC-108-2, AC-108-3) so the next validator sees the closure path.
Run the declared proof target(s), plus any targeted audit-named live/managed-resource proof: cargo test -p handshake-native (full suite -j 2) ; per-item targeted tests enumerated at claim time
If a real external resource or GUI/GPU proof cannot run, record a typed blocker such as NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF or BLOCKED instead of writing PASS/GREEN language.

Only after implementation/proof succeeds, update implementation_result or implementation_evidence, emit the required builder-ready receipt if this lane requires it, and move status to READY_FOR_VALIDATION while leaving validator_verdict as PENDING for the official validator.
